title: Quigley's Anglo-American Establishment
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Quigley's Anglo-American Establishment, about late 19th–20th century at United States (no place named), and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: talks about how US intelligence agencies were birthed out of this kind of round table culture between secret societies in the US and the UK

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a book called The Anglo-American Establishment by a writer named Carroll Quigley, which deals with figures such as Cecil Rhodes and Alfred Milner. Michels says the book describes how American spy agencies grew out of a culture of "round table" groups and secret societies linking the United States and Britain, which would mean those agencies have older, hidden roots.
